subject: Archaeology
title: ROVs and AUVs: Robots in the Deep
description: A quick, practical guide to ROVs and AUVs: Robots in the Deep.

hook.text: Robots now explore shipwrecks at depths where humans cannot survive — mapping sites no diver will ever reach.

buildup.text: ROVs (Remotely Operated Vehicles) are tethered robots with cameras and manipulator arms controlled from the surface.

discovery.text: AUVs (Autonomous Underwater Vehicles) swim independently, scanning vast areas of seabed with sonar and cameras.

twist.text: An AUV found the Endurance at 10,000 feet. It operated under Antarctic ice where no human could have searched.

climax.text: Deep-sea robots are discovering wrecks faster than archaeologists can study them. The technology outpaces the workforce.

punchline.text: Robots can now find wrecks anywhere. The hard part is having enough humans to study them.

quiz.question: What is the difference between ROVs and AUVs?
options: ROVs work only in freshwater while AUVs work in saltwater
ROVs are tethered and controlled from the surface; AUVs swim independently
ROVs are used for photography while AUVs are used for excavation

details.summary: Remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) have extended underwater archaeology into depths no diver can reach. These robots can photograph, map, and even excavate at depths exceeding 4,000 meters, making the deep ocean accessible for the first time.
details.whyItMatters: Most of the ocean floor is beyond human diving limits. ROVs and AUVs opened the remaining 95% of the seabed to archaeological investigation, leading to discoveries like the Titanic, Bismarck, and Endurance in the deep ocean.
takeaways: ROVs are remotely operated; AUVs navigate autonomously
They can work at depths exceeding 4,000 meters
Robots made the deep ocean accessible to archaeology

faq.question: What is the difference between an ROV and an AUV?
faq.answer: ROVs are connected to a surface vessel by a tether and controlled in real-time by an operator. AUVs are untethered and follow pre-programmed routes autonomously, collecting data for later analysis. ROVs offer more control; AUVs cover more area independently.

faq.question: Can underwater robots excavate sites?
faq.answer: Increasingly, yes. Advanced ROVs can use manipulator arms to recover artifacts, position equipment, and clear sediment. However, the fine motor control needed for delicate excavation remains challenging. Most deep-water archaeology focuses on documentation rather than excavation.
